failures.root_cause: Normal wear; alignment drifted after base bolt loosening
failures.repair_action: Replaced coupling insert, re-torqued base bolts, laser alignment

failures.root_cause: Fan cover clogged with coconut fibre and fat mist
failures.repair_action: Cleaned fan cover and fins, checked current and insulation

failures.root_cause: Grease washed out by washdown water; lubrication interval missed
failures.repair_action: Replaced vibrator motor bearings, regreased, fitted splash guard

failures.symptom: Mesh blinded, overflow at screen inlet
failures.root_cause: Coconut cream/oil build-up after VCO line washdown
failures.repair_action: Hot-water and degreaser cleaning of mesh; changed cleaning to every shift

failures.symptom: Seal leak above 20 drops/min, reservoir level falling
failures.root_cause: Abrasive fibre at seal faces; seal at end of life
failures.repair_action: Replaced tandem mechanical seal and reservoir fluid; seal out of stock – emergency purchase

failures.symptom: Seal leak alarm; water found in oil chamber
failures.root_cause: Grit and fibre wear on lower seal faces
failures.repair_action: Lifted pump, replaced upper and lower seal set and oil, megger test OK

failures.symptom: Motor tripped, one phase current zero
failures.root_cause: Loose terminal lug due to vibration and humidity
failures.repair_action: Re-terminated cable, replaced gland set, thermal check

failures.root_cause: Rainy season humidity in store; no anti-condensation protection
failures.repair_action: Dried out in oven by contractor; IR recovered to 450 MΩ; stored with silica gel and cover

failures.root_cause: Rags and fibre wrapped on impeller
failures.repair_action: Lifted pump, removed rags, checked rotation and current

failures.root_cause: Ageing of isolation mounts
failures.repair_action: Replaced isolation springs/mounts set

failures.root_cause: Grease degradation and fibre ingress; bearing near end of life
failures.repair_action: Replaced DE and NDE pump bearings, checked shaft and alignment

failures.symptom: Backflow into sump when pump stops
failures.root_cause: Flapper hinge pin worn
failures.repair_action: Replaced DN100 swing check valve (last unit in stock)

failures.symptom: Hole in mesh (approx. 40 mm); fibre found downstream
failures.root_cause: Mesh fatigue at clamp line; over-tensioning
failures.repair_action: Replaced mesh panel and clamps; SC-101B carried full load during repair

failures.failure_mode: Impeller and wear ring wear + shaft sleeve scoring
failures.root_cause: Abrasive wear after 9 years; 3rd failure in 12 months
failures.repair_action: Pump removed; SP-P01 installed at P-101A position 2026-04-21; unit assessed Replace (Batch 2.D); new pump installed 2026-06-15

failures.symptom: Failed to start – motor locked-rotor trip
failures.failure_mode: Seized shaft – stuck seal faces after 7 weeks idle
failures.root_cause: Rotation skipped 7 weeks and no standby inspection; seal faces bonded
failures.repair_action: Freed shaft, replaced tandem seal, test run; back in service 2026-04-20 11:40

failures.root_cause: Abrasive wear of channel impeller
failures.repair_action: Replaced impeller and O-ring kit; flow restored to 50 m³/h

failures.symptom: Mesh blinded by cream; inlet overflowing
failures.root_cause: Coconut cream surge from VCO line upset
failures.repair_action: Emergency cleaning; VCO line informed

failures.root_cause: Cable abraded on sump edge
failures.repair_action: Replaced power cable and entry kit; added cable guard

failures.root_cause: Moisture ingress at terminal box; burnt winding
failures.repair_action: Installed spare SP-VM01; failed motor sent for rewinding (contractor)

failures.root_cause: O-ring hardening on outer seal
failures.repair_action: Replaced gasket set and topped up reservoir; seal monitored

failures.root_cause: Normal wear after 9 years
failures.repair_action: Replaced motor DE and NDE bearings

failures.root_cause: Fixing bolts loosened by vibration
failures.repair_action: Re-set and torqued eccentric weights, new cover gasket

procedureSteps.instruction: Start the standby unit (OP-03 step 2) to keep the flow going
procedureSteps.safety_note: If standby fails: go to EM-06

procedureSteps.instruction: Stop and isolate the vibrating unit (ISO steps)
Check coupling, base bolts, guard contact and debris; turn shaft by hand
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Note: loose bolts / worn insert / rubbing / clogging

procedureSteps.instruction: Review the last 14 days of vibration and temperature trend on the tablet
Correct simple causes (tighten bolts, replace coupling insert PR-14, clear debris)
If bearing or impeller damage is suspected, raise corrective WO (PR-06 / PR-09) and inform engineer
Estimate leak rate and check the seal reservoir level
If ≤ 5 drops/min and level stable: keep running, check every round
If above limit: start standby, then stop and isolate leaking unit
Check spare seal stock; if 0 → emergency purchase (+30%, supplier list)
Replace seal (PR-07 transfer pump / PR-17 submersible)
Record leak history; if 2nd seal failure in 12 months → repair-or-replace review
Start standby unit
Isolate the clogged unit (ISO steps); for submersible lift it out (PR-16)
procedureSteps.safety_note: Rags and fibre may hide sharp objects – cut-resistant gloves

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove rags/fibre from impeller, strainer or suction
Check screens upstream for mesh holes or bypass (SV-01)
Return to service (OP-05); report if screens let solids through
Check EQ tank level and suction valve position
If level low: reduce pump flow (throttle discharge) or stop until level recovers
If level normal: clean suction strainer (SV-02)
Record event; check impeller at next shutdown if cavitation lasted > 1 h
Start standby unit
Isolate the tripped unit (ISO steps)
Turn shaft by hand; check for clogging or seizure
Check supply voltage on all 3 phases and overload setting
Megger motor windings (electrician)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: ≥ 100 MΩ ready; < 5 MΩ → do not restart

procedureSteps.instruction: Reset only after cause is found; one reset attempt; else escalate
Inform shift supervisor and wastewater engineer immediately (pair may be down)
Check panel: breaker, overload, control fuse, selector switch
Isolate unit; turn shaft by hand
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Seized → go to EM-09 escalation and PR-07; free → electrical check

procedureSteps.instruction: If the duty unit can run safely at reduced load, keep it running while repair proceeds
Check when the unit last ran and was checked (rotation, standby check); record as lesson
Check fan cover and cooling fins for fibre/fat build-up
Measure current on all phases
If blocked: switch to standby, isolate, clean fan cover (PR fan check)
If current high: check pump for clogging (EM-03)
Do not touch; switch off from the MCC; call electrician and supervisor
procedureSteps.safety_note: Fire risk: CO2 extinguisher only; never water on live equipment

procedureSteps.instruction: Start standby unit if its circuit is separate and safe
Electrician inspects cable, terminal box and starter
Megger before any restart; raise corrective WO
Call wastewater engineer, shift supervisor and production manager; start the incident on the tablet
Read EQ (or sump) level and inflow; tablet shows buffer time
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Buffer time known (EQ ≈ 2.5 h; sump ≈ 12 min)

procedureSteps.instruction: Ask production to curtail lines in order VCO+flour → DC → coconut water as level approaches high-high
procedureSteps.safety_note: Bypass only with engineer approval – RA 9275 fines

procedureSteps.instruction: Repair the quicker unit first (EM-06 / EM-01); consider installing stored spare (OP-04)
When restored: restart lines; draft incident report on the tablet
Confirm level reading against the sight gauge (SV-05)
Check that the duty pump is running at full flow; start standby in parallel if allowed
Ask production to curtail washdown/CIP first, then lines (EM-09)
Record peak level and duration
Inform wastewater engineer and production manager: plant stop is required
Production stops lines in order; utilities continue
Repair the quicker screen first (SV-01 mesh, SV-03 vibrator motor)
Restart production after one screen is proven (OP-05)
Open the Repair_vs_Replace result on the tablet for the asset
Check the facts: failures in 12 months, age, repair cost vs new, downtime cost from Batch 1
Check a spare or swap-in is available while deciding
Record decision (Repair / Repair – watch / Replace), reason and approver
Confirm the part ID, quantity and that no compatible part is in stock
Call suppliers on the Suppliers list (public contacts); record price and delivery time
Get approval for the emergency premium (assumed +30% + freight)
Raise the order; set reorder point review
Check part number, quantity and documents against the order
Check for damage; for seals and bearings keep sealed packing
Book into stock; label location; update Spare_Parts_Inventory
Check the repair record and test results
Preserve (PR-22 pump / MO-10 motor)
Set location and status in Equipment_Register and Spare_Readiness
Read the draft; check facts, times and costs against the records
Confirm root cause and add corrective actions with owners and due dates
Approve and sign; corrective actions appear as tasks
Review PM done on time %, overdue tasks, missed rounds, rotation compliance
Review failures, downtime, repair cost and spare readiness
Agree actions; record in the meeting note
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Disconnect the motor cables at the terminal box (or test from the starter with cable included – note which)
Apply 500 V DC phase-to-earth for 1 minute; record reading and winding temperature
procedureSteps.safety_note: Discharge the winding to earth after each test

procedureSteps.instruction: Optional: read again at 10 minutes and work out the polarization index (10-min ÷ 1-min)
Compare with plant rule and the last result
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: ≥ 100 MΩ = Ready; 5–100 MΩ = watch / dry out; < 5 MΩ = Not ready

procedureSteps.instruction: Reconnect (correct phase order), close terminal box, remove locks; record result in the tablet
Check the nameplate/lubrication plate: grease type, quantity per bearing, interval. Sealed (2Z/2RS) bearings are NOT greased
Wipe the grease nipples and the gun nozzle clean
procedureSteps.safety_note: Dirt pushed into a bearing shortens its life

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove the grease drain plug (if fitted)
Add the specified quantity slowly to the DE bearing, then the NDE bearing (count gun strokes – 1 stroke ≈ value marked on gun)
Run the motor 15–30 min with the drain open so old grease can purge, then refit plug
Check bearing temperature after 1 h
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Temperature back to normal (< 80 °C); short rise after greasing is normal

procedureSteps.instruction: Record date, grease used and quantity
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Disconnect cables; uncouple; move the motor to the workshop
Remove fan cover and fan; mark end shields; remove end shields and rotor
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Rotor out without touching the winding

procedureSteps.instruction: Pull bearings with a puller
Heat new bearings (≈ 110 °C) and fit to the shoulder; fill with grease if open type
Refit rotor, end shields (to marks), fan and cover; turn shaft by hand
Megger (MO-01); reinstall, align (PR-15), test run (OP-05)
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove fan cover
Clean fan, cover grille and frame fins of fibre and fat
procedureSteps.safety_note: Do not wash with water jets

procedureSteps.instruction: Check fan blades for cracks and the cover for dents touching the fan
Refit cover; turn shaft by hand
Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners

procedureSteps.instruction: Start the motor and record readings; Run 30 min: frame temperature normal
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA
procedureSteps.safety_note: Stand clear of coupling during start

procedureSteps.instruction: Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Open the terminal box; look for burn marks, discoloured lugs, moisture
Re-torque terminal nuts to the motor maker's value
Check the gland seals the cable; replace the gasket if hard or cracked
procedureSteps.safety_note: Wet area – water entry causes earth faults

procedureSteps.instruction: Close box with all screws
Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners

procedureSteps.instruction: Start the motor and record readings; Run 15 min: current balanced
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA
procedureSteps.safety_note: Stand clear of coupling during start

procedureSteps.instruction: Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock
Isolate the starter from its supply (LOTO at the incomer); verify 0 V
Check overload setting against motor full-load current (M-101: 12.8 A)
procedureSteps.safety_note: Never raise the setting to stop nuisance trips

procedureSteps.instruction: Inspect contactor contacts and coil terminals for pitting, heat marks
Replace worn contactor or overload relay
Restore supply; start motor; measure current on 3 phases
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the motor; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Disconnect and mark cables; uncouple; remove the failed motor
Check the spare: Spare_Readiness Ready; megger ≥ 100 MΩ
Install spare; fit coupling hub; connect cables in the marked order
Align to pump (PR-15)
Bump-start (1–2 s) uncoupled or with guard on; check rotation against the pump arrow
procedureSteps.safety_note: Wrong rotation can unscrew an impeller

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove tools; refit guards; open isolation valves; remove locks in reverse order (each person removes own lock)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Guards fitted; all locks removed by owners

procedureSteps.instruction: Start the motor and record readings; Run 30 min: flow, pressure, current, vibration and bearing temperature normal
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Within limits: vibration < 4.5 mm/s, bearing < 80 °C, current ≤ 105% FLA
procedureSteps.safety_note: Stand clear of coupling during start

procedureSteps.instruction: Record parts used and hours in the work order; attach photos; update spare stock
Isolate and remove the motor to the workshop (or stores)
Open terminal box and drain plugs; heat the winding gently (oven or lamps) – keep below about 90 °C
Megger every 4 h and record; continue until readings stop rising
Accept when ≥ 100 MΩ (corrected to the same temperature)
Store with silica gel and cover (MO-10); update Spare_Readiness
Start the partner unit and confirm it runs normally
Stop the vibrator motors; lock and tag the MCC breaker (each worker own lock)
Try to start (try-out); electrician checks 0 V at the motor terminals
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Does not start; 0 V all phases
procedureSteps.safety_note: Test the meter on a live source first

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove eccentric weight covers; check both weights are at the same setting on both motors and both shaft ends
Check mounting bolts for torque and frame welds for cracks
Grease bearings if regreasable (MO-02); replace bearing set if noisy
Refit weight covers with new gaskets
Start; confirm the two motors turn in opposite directions; measure current
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Opposite rotation; current ≈ 3.2 A each, balanced

procedureSteps.instruction: Store indoors, dry, off the floor, away from vibration; cover with silica gel inside the cover
Monthly: turn the shaft by hand several turns to move the grease
Quarterly: megger (MO-01)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: ≥ 100 MΩ Ready; < 5 MΩ Not ready → MO-08

procedureSteps.instruction: Record in Spare_Readiness
With the motor running at normal load, measure the 3 line currents
procedureSteps.safety_note: Live work – electrician only, insulated PPE

procedureSteps.instruction: Measure the 3 line voltages at the starter
Work out the imbalance (largest difference from average ÷ average)
If above limit: raise a work order (MO-05, MO-06)
Check the seal lubricant reservoir level and the casing for leaks
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Reservoir level in normal band; no leaks

procedureSteps.instruction: Open suction valve fully; set discharge valve about one quarter open
procedureSteps.safety_note: Never start against a closed suction valve

procedureSteps.instruction: Confirm pump casing is full of liquid (vent until liquid appears)
Start the motor; within 10 s open the discharge valve slowly to full
procedureSteps.safety_note: Stop at once if no pressure in 30 s (dry running)

procedureSteps.instruction: Check rotation, noise and seal; take current with clamp meter
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Current ≈ 11.5 A (≤ 12.8 A FLA); no abnormal noise

procedureSteps.instruction: Record start time and readings in the round on the tablet
If this is a changeover, start the partner pump first (OP-01) and confirm flow
Close the discharge valve slowly
Stop the motor; confirm the shaft stops without reverse rotation
procedureSteps.safety_note: If shaft runs backwards, check valve has failed – raise work order

procedureSteps.instruction: Leave suction valve open (standby) or close it (maintenance)
Record stop time and reason
Open today's rotation on the tablet; confirm which unit becomes duty
Start the standby unit (OP-01 for transfer pumps; local start for sump pump or screen)
procedureSteps.safety_note: If it fails to start: stop and use EM-06

procedureSteps.instruction: Stop the former duty unit (OP-02) and leave it in standby
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Former duty unit idle, valves set for standby

procedureSteps.instruction: Confirm changeover on the tablet; the system clears the missed-rotation alert
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: Rotation logged with time and initials
procedureSteps.safety_note: Never skip – a standby left idle for weeks may not start

procedureSteps.instruction: Check Spare_Readiness: status Ready, last IR test and preservation record
procedureSteps.safety_note: Do not install a Not ready spare

procedureSteps.instruction: Remove preservation (covers, desiccant); turn shaft by hand
Install the spare (PR-02/PR-03 for transfer pump; PR-16 for submersible)
Megger the motor before first start
Run test (OP-05)
Update Equipment_Register location and Spare_Readiness (spare now in service); order repair of removed unit
Start unit; listen for rubbing or knocking for the first minute
procedureSteps.safety_note: Stop at once on abnormal noise

procedureSteps.instruction: After 15 min take vibration on DE and NDE bearings (horizontal and vertical)
After 30 min take bearing temperatures and motor current
Check seal (transfer pumps) or flow/current (submersibles)
procedureSteps.acceptance_criteria: No visible leak; flow within 10% of rated

procedureSteps.instruction: Record readings as the new baseline for the unit
Confirm EQ tank level is above pump centreline (flooded suction)
Open suction valve; open casing vent slowly

procedureKeyPoints.text: Insulation falls slowly with moisture and dirt; testing finds it before an earth fault or burnt winding.
Old grease loses its oil and collects dirt; fresh grease keeps the bearings cool. Bearing failure is the most common motor failure.
Worn motor bearings cause noise, vibration and heat, and can let the rotor rub the stator.
A damp winding can recover if dried properly; burning it out costs a rewind.
The two vibrator motors make the linear screen motion only when matched and turning in opposite directions.
Worn bearings cause most vibration and heat problems; a bad fit ruins a new bearing in weeks.
The tandem seal keeps acidic wastewater in; the reservoir lubricant cools the seals and warns of a failing inner seal.
A worn impeller lowers flow and head and can cause vibration.
Misalignment is a main cause of seal and bearing failure and vibration.
The submersible sits under wastewater; it must be lifted out safely for any work.
The oil chamber protects the motor; water in the oil is the early warning of a failing lower seal.
Restores the pump to as-new condition when the repair-or-replace review says Repair.
A new pump only proves itself with checks and a baseline; the baseline is used for every later comparison.
A worn submersible impeller lowers flow so the sump fills faster.
A hole in the mesh lets fibre reach the EQ tank and the transfer pumps (seal and impeller damage).
A failed check valve lets water flow back and spins the pump backwards.
Test at about 500 V DC for motors up to 1 kV; record the winding temperature with the result (IEEE 43).
Check the lubrication plate: grease type, quantity, interval. Sealed bearings are NOT greased.
Mark end shields before removing; protect the winding when pulling the rotor.
Heat gently, keep below about 90 °C, megger every 4 h.
Set both eccentric weights equal on both motors and both ends.
Heat with an induction heater to about 110 °C and push straight to the shoulder.
Check the drained lubricant: grey or watery = the inner seal was leaking.
Measure vane wear and wear-ring gap and record them – they feed the repair-or-replace decision.
Check soft foot first (PR-04); move the motor, not the pump.
Lift only by the chain/handle along the guide rails.
Tsurumi interval: every 1,500 h or 6 months (plant: quarterly).
Lay out parts in order, photograph as found, measure everything before cleaning.
Megger before first start; bump-start to check rotation.
Check the oil chamber at the same time (PR-17).
Switch the flow to the other screen first (SV-08).
Isolate both sides and drain before opening.
Compare with the last result – a big drop matters even above 100 MΩ.
Open the drain plug and run the motor so old grease can purge.
Heat new bearings with an induction heater.
Accept only when readings stop rising and are ≥ 100 MΩ at the same temperature.
After work, check opposite rotation and balanced current (≈ 3.2 A each).
Using a flame, or hammering the outer ring – both damage the bearing.
Grease or dirt on the seal faces – one grain makes a leak path.
Hammering the impeller off – use the puller.
Aligning with a soft foot – readings change when bolts are tightened.
Lift by the power cable or stand under the load.
Use turbine oil ISO VG32 – quantity per Tsurumi manual (verify).
Replace all wear parts in one go – bearings, seals, sleeve, wear ring, gaskets, coupling insert.
Save the 4-hour run readings and performance check as the new baseline.
Megger motor and cable before reinstalling: ≥ 20 MΩ.
Tension the clamps evenly.
After repair, stop the pump and confirm the shaft stays still.
Test a motor that is not locked out, or touch the leads before discharging.
Over-greasing – too much grease churns and overheats the bearing.
Forgetting to megger and re-align after the job.
SP-M01 dropped to 3.2 MΩ in Aug 2025 and recovered to 450 MΩ after drying.
Changing one motor's weights only – the screen twists and welds crack.
Not checking shaft seats – a worn seat lets the new bearing creep.
Starting without venting – the new seal runs dry and cracks in seconds.
Forgetting to reset the impeller clearance (PR-10) after fitting.
Not re-checking after tightening the feet.
Enter the sump without a confined-space permit.
Topping up milky oil instead of replacing the seals.
Re-using worn parts 'because they look OK' – measure against limits.
Skipping pipe-strain check – flanges must line up without force.
Not setting the impeller-to-suction-cover clearance (verify in Tsurumi manual).
Over-tensioning – tears start at the clamp line.
Opening the valve cover under pressure.
Mix grease types; use a dirty nipple or gun.
Guess the seal setting length or impeller nut torque – use the KSB manual.

questions.question: Is the reading 7.1 mm/s or more, or did the unit trip?
Has vibration risen more than 1 mm/s in the last 7 days?
questions.if_no: Action: monitor every round; recheck in 24 h

questions.question: Are base bolts or coupling loose or worn?
questions.if_yes: Action: tighten / replace insert (PR-14), then align (PR-15)

questions.question: Is the bearing temperature 80 °C or more?
questions.if_yes: Action: plan bearing replacement (PR-06) within 24 h
questions.if_no: Action: check impeller for wear or clogging (PR-09 / EM-03)

questions.question: Is the leak more than 5 drops per minute?
Is the seal reservoir level falling?
questions.if_no: Action: monitor; plan seal replacement at next shutdown

questions.question: Is a spare seal set in stock?
questions.if_no: Action: emergency purchase (supplier list), keep unit on standby

questions.question: Is the pump current higher than normal?
Are rags or fibre found at the impeller or strainer?
Does the shaft turn backwards after stopping?
questions.if_no: Action: check rotation direction and air lock (OP-06)

questions.question: Is the overload or breaker tripped?
Does the shaft turn freely by hand (after isolation)?
questions.if_no: Action: seized – escalate; free shaft and replace seal (PR-07)

questions.question: Is there power at the panel and control circuit?
questions.if_yes: Action: check selector switch and level control

questions.question: Is this the standby and the duty unit has failed?
Does it trip again within 5 minutes after one reset?
questions.if_yes: Action: do not reset again; escalate (EM-05)

questions.question: Are the three phase currents balanced within 10%?
questions.if_no: Action: electrician checks supply and terminals (EM-05)

questions.question: Is the fan cover blocked with fibre or fat?
Is the motor current above 105% of full-load current?
Is there smoke or visible sparks?
questions.if_yes: Action: switch off at MCC; escalate; fire procedure (EM-08)

questions.question: Is the cable sheath damaged?
questions.if_no: Action: megger motor; lift pump and inspect (PR-17)

questions.question: Is the EQ tank level below 30%?
questions.if_yes: Action: throttle or stop pump until level recovers (EM-04)

questions.question: Is the sump level rising while the pump is off?
Is the other screen running and clean?
questions.if_yes: Action: switch to it (SV-08) and clean this screen (SV-07)
questions.if_no: Action: clean in place now; tell production (possible upset)

questions.question: Is the hole larger than the mesh opening (solids passing)?
Is the other screen available?
Does the transmitter agree with the sight gauge within 5%?
Are both pumps of the pair available?
questions.if_yes: Action: run duty at full flow; ask production to cut washdown (EM-10)

questions.question: Will the buffer run out within 1 hour?
questions.if_no: Action: repair quicker unit; consider stored spare (OP-04)

questions.question: Is the oil milky or does it contain water drops?
Is the noise from the coupling area?

incidentReports.expected_report_text: On 2026-08-18 at 10:05, VM-101B (Vibrator motor set for SC-101B (2 × 0.75 kW)) had a failure: winding failure. It was detected by trip: vibrator motor overheating and trip. The standby unit took over, so there was no production impact. Root cause: moisture ingress at terminal box; burnt winding. Repair: Installed spare SP-VM01; failed motor sent for rewinding (contractor). Downtime of the asset: 26 h; repair cost PHP 22,550. Repair-or-replace result: Repair. Action: Replace terminal gaskets yearly.
